gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 23?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 23 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from multiple models, including GFS runs, indicate Munich's August 23 high will hover near the 1991–2020 climatological average of 23.5°C under mostly clear to partly cloudy skies with light northerly winds and negligible precipitation. This tight clustering around 22–23°C explains the near-even market-implied odds, as small differences in daytime insolation, boundary-layer mixing, or minor advection from surrounding high pressure can shift the peak by 1°C. Historical analogs show late-August maxima routinely vary ±2°C day-to-day, while official DWD and ECMWF guidance released in the past 24 hours has shown minimal run-to-run spread, leaving traders with limited new data to differentiate the two leading outcomes before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders price Tokyo’s August 23 maximum near 30–31 °C because Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble forecasts indicate a cloudy day with scattered showers or thundery activity that will limit afternoon heating. Typical late-August climatology shows a 30.5 °C normal high, yet persistent cloud cover and precipitation reduce insolation enough to cap peaks at or below 31 °C on most model runs. Differentiating the tightly bunched 30 °C (40 %) and 31 °C (35 %) outcomes hinges on the exact timing and coverage of showers: earlier or heavier rain suppresses the peak toward 30 °C, while delayed or lighter activity allows brief clearing that pushes the official reading to 31 °C. Lower-probability 32 °C scenarios require stronger subsidence and reduced moisture than currently modeled, while sub-29 °C outcomes remain unlikely absent an unforecasted cold front. Updated JMA guidance and real-time observations through the afternoon will resolve the remaining uncertainty before market settlement.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders price Tokyo’s August 23 maximum near 30–31 °C because Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble forecasts indicate a cloudy day with scattered showers or thundery activity that will limit afternoon heating. Typical late-August climatology shows a 30.5 °C normal high, yet persistent cloud cover and precipitation reduce insolation enough to cap peaks at or below 31 °C on most model runs. Differentiating the tightly bunched 30 °C (40 %) and 31 °C (35 %) outcomes hinges on the exact timing and coverage of showers: earlier or heavier rain suppresses the peak toward 30 °C, while delayed or lighter activity allows brief clearing that pushes the official reading to 31 °C. Lower-probability 32 °C scenarios require stronger subsidence and reduced moisture than currently modeled, while sub-29 °C outcomes remain unlikely absent an unforecasted cold front. Updated JMA guidance and real-time observations through the afternoon will resolve the remaining uncertainty before market settlement.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and supporting numerical models indicate a Tokyo daytime maximum near 31°C on August 23 under mostly cloudy skies, scattered showers, and light northeasterly winds near the seasonal climatological average of 30.7°C. Recent observations show midday temperatures approaching 30°C with high humidity around 70% and dew points near 24°C, while persistent cloud cover and precipitation chances of 20–30% limit intense solar heating and convective buildup that could push readings higher. Ensemble guidance shows limited spread around this outcome, consistent with recent days’ pattern of 31–33°C highs, though brief afternoon clearing could allow a one-degree upward nudge before evening cooling sets in.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and major models indicate a high of 32–35°C for Tokyo on August 25, 2026, with most guidance clustering around 33–34°C under partly cloudy to mostly sunny conditions.** Southerly flow ahead of a weakening frontal boundary is advecting warm, humid maritime air, while limited cloud cover and light winds allow strong daytime heating. Recent model runs show modest spread driven by small differences in predicted cloud timing and any weak afternoon showers, which could shave 1–2°C off the peak if they develop earlier than expected.

The flat 18.5% probabilities across 30–33°C reflect this narrow but unresolved uncertainty band in ensemble guidance, consistent with typical 48-hour forecast variability for maximum temperature in a humid subtropical summer regime. Historical late-August climatology (average high near 30–31°C) places the current setup above normal, supporting the market’s emphasis on the upper-30s range while leaving room for resolution shifts from the next model cycle or updated JMA guidance.
